evidence_occurrences.evidence_text:
Testing / developing algorithms:
When testing algorithms, I used the last four years of the training dataset (after removing them from the data I was using for training) to test against. While this worked well in the initial stages, I found that once my leaderboard MASE got below about 2.05, this ‘training MASE’ became a much less reliable indicator of whether the leaderboard MASE would increase or decrease with a change. So, during the last few weeks of the contest, I primarily made small tweaks, and tested their value by submitting a new prediction to Kaggle rather than comparing my MASE results. I believe that this indicates a significant difference in nature of the last 4 years of the training set compared to the 4 years in the test set. If the test set includes data from 2008-2009, I’m speculating that depressed tourism numbers as a result of the global economic recession could have caused a significant difference in the trends.

lessons.title: Distinguish algorithm quality from shared test-era trends
lessons.statement: When many forecast series may share the same test dates, proposed reuse: Proposed conditional application: Assess performance over staggered historical cutoff periods before claiming one method generally better. Proposed check: Evaluate rolling and staggered origins across several eras and compare method rankings, horizon error and sensitivity to shared shocks. Limitation: Source did not perform the suggested staggered evaluation; common test-era confounding is a hypothesis.

lessons.statement: When rare high labels dominate error and may shift across years, proposed reuse: Proposed conditional application: Investigate extreme-target distribution shift before adding a special tail class or removing suspect rows. Limitation: Genuine extreme weather must not be deleted solely for leaderboard improvement; 2014 labels unavailable to author.
